articles.headline: Maikel Garcia trade grades: Mariners land Gold Glove infielder; Royals get pitching help, but with huge risks
keyFacts: The Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners agreed to a six-player trade involving infielder Maikel Garcia and several pitchers, according to reports.
ESPN reported that the Mariners will acquire third baseman Maikel Garcia, while the Seattle Times reported the Royals will receive Logan Evans, Bryce Miller, and Jose A. Ferrer.
Neither team has officially announced the trade yet.
body: The Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade. The Mariners are set to acquire third baseman Maikel Garcia in a six-player trade, reports ESPN. The Royals will receive righties Logan Evans and Bryce Miller, and lefty Jose A. Ferrer, in the deal, according to the Seattle Times. Neither team has announced the trade.
Here are the full trade details:

Garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense. He is a year removed from a 5.6 WAR season and receiving MVP votes. Garcia is signed long-term as well. He's owed a very reasonable $52.5 million through 2030, with a club option for 2031.

The 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City. An oblique strain delayed the start to his 2026 season, but once healthy, he threw 118 ⅔ innings with a 4.17 ERA and under-the-hood numbers that were hit (3.70 expected ERA) or miss (4.41 FIP). Miller threw 180 ⅓ innings with a 2.94 ERA in 2024, and will remain under team control through 2029.

Ferrer, 26, is a workhorse ground ball reliever with three years of control remaining. McArthur (fracture) and Evans (Tommy John) both missed 2026 with elbow surgery. McArthur pitched in four minor-league rehab games in September and should be ready for spring training. Evans has surgery in January and is expected back at midseason.
Here now are our grades for this three-for-three swap between 2027 American League postseason hopefuls.
Seattle Mariners: A

The Mariners came into the offseason with an opening at third base, a glaring need to improve their defense, and more starters than rotation spots. That all came to a head in this trade. They used Miller, their least effective starter the last two seasons, and two spare parts to net a long-term solution at the hot corner in Garcia, who plays Gold Glove-caliber defense.

One player alone won't fix Seattle's defense, of course, but Garcia is a very big step toward improving a unit that ranked 26th in defensive runs saved and 30th (by a lot) in outs above average. As for the lineup, new manager Jason Kanzler can run out something like this most days:
- DH Brendan Donovan, LHB
- CF Julio Rodríguez, RHB
- RF Dominic Canzone, LHB
- C Cal Raleigh, SHB
- 1B Josh Naylor, LHB
- 3B Maikel Garcia, RHB
- LF Luke Raley, LHB
- 2B Cole Young, LHB
- SS Colt Emerson, LHB

Donovan was limited to 39 games by two groin strains and a concussion this past season. He's very versatile and needn't be locked into DH. The Mariners can play Donovan in the outfield to open up DH at-bats for slugger Lazaro Montes, who hit some titanic home runs during his MLB debut in 2026. They could also move Donovan around to give others DH days.

The lineup and the defense are improved, and the Mariners still have a formidable rotation that includes Kade Anderson, Logan Gilbert, Emerson Hancock, George Kirby, and Bryan Woo. Right-hander Ryan Sloan, arguably the top pitching prospect in baseball (it's either Sloan or Anderson), is knocking on the door and figures to debut at some point in 2027.

Seattle will miss Ferrer in their bullpen but also have close to an entire offseason (minus a lockout) to replace him. Assuming the Mariners won't break the bank for Adrian Morejon, the free agent market still offers solid second- and third-tier lefty reliever options in A.J. Minter, Sean Newcomb, JoJo Romero, Gregory Soto, and Alex Vesia. Ferrer is a quality reliever but not irreplaceable.

Before his elbow fracture, which ultimately required three surgeries, McArthur showed a very lively curveball and strong ground ball ability. He's a middle reliever more than a high-leverage option, but is not merely a throw-in. Langevin struck out 106 batters in 55 ⅓ Single-A relief innings thanks to his mid-90s fastball in 2026. He also walked 39 batters, however.

Garcia received MVP votes a year ago thanks to a .286/.351/.449 line with 16 home runs and 23 stolen bases. He also runs some of the game's best contact rates. That's his upside and maybe 2025 was a career year, but Garcia has a reasonably high floor thanks to his defense. Getting even league-average offense moving forward makes this a win for Seattle.
Kansas City Royals: C
Desperation for pitching transparent in risky return

The free agent market is flush with No. 3-4 type starters and light on position players, specifically non-first base infielders. Couldn't the Royals keep Garcia and just sign a pitcher or two? There is something to be said for Miller's cost control as an arbitration-eligible player, of course, but he hasn't been healthy and effective at the same time since 2024. That's awfully risky.

Evans is a quality second piece as long as he bounces back well from Tommy John surgery. He made his MLB debut with the Mariners in 2025 and underwhelmed (4.32 ERA with iffy underlying numbers in 81 ⅓ innings), though he was regarded as a strong prospect before that, someone who should hold down a rotation spot for a long time.
Here's what FanGraphs wrote about Evans in June 2025, the last time he was prospect-eligible:

(His) sweeper is easily his best pitch, spins in at 2,800 rpm, and has hellacious lateral wipe. His reliance on it robs it of some bat-missing ability, and the last couple of years, the miss rate on Evans' slider has been pretty average because he's so often trying to throw it for strikes and hitters anticipate its arrival. But because Evans' fastball is fairly vulnerable, he's forced to lean on his breaking stuff ... Again, it's really only the sweeper that's plus, but Evans has a super deep repertoire, he throws a good rate of strikes and gets groundballs, and in 2024, he proved he could sustain this kind of stuff across more than 100 innings. Without a single pitch generating plus miss, he's probably not going to be a star, but he does enough to be a useful member of a big league rotation in a no. 4/5 capacity.

The Royals will have to wait for Evans to make an impact in their uniform because the timing of his Tommy John surgery means his rehab will extend into next spring and summer, but he is a quality second piece even if he is only a No. 4-5 starter. Cheap back-end starters are incredibly valuable and Evans should be that once his elbow is ready to go.

Ferrer could very well wind up closing games for the Royals this season and is a quality add to the bullpen. For Kansas City, the trade boils down to three things. One, can they keep Miller healthy and get him back to his 2024 form? He's the headliner in the trade and his success is imperative. Two, will Evans turn into a reliable rotation member once his elbow is sound?

And three, was Nick Loftin's 2026 for real? The Royals believe it was, hence trading Garcia. Loftin, 28, was a Gold Glove finalist this past season and he authored a .240/.322/.388 batting line with eight home runs in 118 games. If you're sold on Loftin as a league-average hitter and Gold Glove-caliber defender, well, that's what Garcia is, just without the name value.

The Royals badly needed rotation help -- there's no arguing that -- but they also ranked 22nd in runs this year and were middle of the pack defensively despite Loftin's (and Garcia's) glovework. There's a chance Kansas City made its position player core worse with only unspectacular pitching upgrades to show for it. I understand what they did. I just don't love it.

articles.headline: As GTA 6 Breaks Records, Rockstar Devs Call for Union Recognition
keyFacts: Rockstar Games animation programmer Nestor Uriarte advocated for unionization in an opinion piece as 1,600 U.K. staff await the results of an ongoing union vote ending Nov. 26.
Uriarte cited concerns over job security, historical allegations of extreme work hours, and the rise of generative AI as reasons for employees to unionize.
The Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain stated that a recognized union contract would provide a framework for negotiating pay, benefits, and AI policies.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 will almost certainly set sales records when it launches tomorrow, Nov. 19. However, despite the windfall for Rockstar Games, many of the studio’s employees remain worried about their jobs. In an opinion piece from The Guardian, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte outlined the benefits of unionization as developers at the studio await the results of an ongoing union vote. 1,600 staff in the U.K. have until Nov. 26 to cast their ballots.
Why Uriarte believes Rockstar employees should unionize
Uriarte points out that Grand Theft Auto 5 has sold over 230 million copies and made $10 billion, surpassing any film in Hollywood history. GTA 6 is expected to break these records.

“Behind these numbers are thousands of people whose talent and hard work make the games possible,” Uriarte writes. “With a recognised union, we can ensure everyone, across every department, sees a fair share of the success we contributed to. Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too.”

Uriarte brings up well-documented allegations that Rockstar has enabled "crunch culture" over the years. In one case, former studio co-head Dan Houser said the game’s writing team worked “100-hour weeks” to release Red Dead Redemption 2 on time. Rockstar has faced similar allegations dating back to 2010, when an anonymous letter from a group of “wives of Rockstar San Diego employees” accused the company’s California studio of forcing staff to work 12-hour days, six days a week to finish the original Red Dead Redemption.

“With a strong union we could make sure there is no return to this system,” Uriarte says. “We have already seen the introduction of some overtime pay, and now we want to keep on pushing to ensure that every hour worked in our industry is an hour paid.”

“After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds,” Uriarte says. “It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.”

Uriarte brings up the latest reason why unions are necessary: generative AI. “The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry. Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI. Rockstar has said it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people. But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together.”
Rockstar and union-busting allegations

The Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain says that if Rockstar recognizes the current union contract, it will “provide a framework for workers to negotiate over pay, including overtime and bonuses, as well as leave and pensions, and to have consultation rights over HR policies and the use of AI.”

Last October, Rockstar was accused of union busting after it fired 34 people, most of whom were involved in organizing the current vote. Rockstar said these employees leaked confidential information on Discord, a claim disputed by several of the dismissed developers, who went on to sue. It seems that by next week we'll know whether Rockstar employees, who helped create one of the biggest and most critically celebrated entertainment projects of all time, will have more leverage in their workplace.

articles.headline: 'Very hard to let Kuldeep go': Sourav Ganguly opens up on Delhi Capitals' big trade for Rishabh Pant
keyFacts: Delhi Capitals head coach Sourav Ganguly stated that parting ways with spinner Kuldeep Yadav for the IPL 2027 season was a very difficult decision.
Kuldeep was traded to Lucknow Super Giants in a deal that brought Rishabh Pant back to Delhi Capitals for Rs 15 crore to strengthen their batting.
Delhi Capitals will head into the December 16 mini-auction with nine slots to fill and Rs 39.50 crore remaining in their purse.
body: Delhi Capitals head coach Sourav Ganguly has admitted that parting ways with Kuldeep Yadav was among the toughest decisions the franchise had to make ahead of the IPL 2027 season, describing the India spinner as a "very special cricketer".

Kuldeep was traded to Lucknow Super Giants in a high-profile deal involving Rishabh Pant, who makes a return to Delhi Capitals at a revised fee of Rs 15 crore. Pant had been signed by LSG for a record Rs 27 crore at the IPL 2025 auction.

Explaining the reasoning behind the trade, Ganguly said Delhi were keen to strengthen their batting resources and viewed Pant's return as an important addition to their squad. However, he acknowledged that letting go of a player of Kuldeep's calibre was never going to be an easy call.

"It was a tough trade because Kuldeep is a very special cricketer. He's been with Delhi Capitals for a long period of time, but in the IPL, with 10 teams, it's always about that one balance factor. And we were looking at a batsman. We got a domestic batsman in Rishabh Pant, who's done well for Delhi. Someone whom I rate very, very highly. But it was very hard to let Kuldeep go, and with Axar and Ashutosh, releasing them was a complete no-no. They are very important part of our squad," Ganguly said on JioStar's 'IPL 2027 Retention Special'.

Kuldeep, who had been retained by Delhi at his existing fee of Rs 13.50 crore, will now begin a new chapter with LSG. Pant, meanwhile, returns to the franchise where he spent eight seasons between 2016 and 2024 and also led the side.

Ganguly also shed light on the wider considerations that went into Delhi's retention and release decisions, stressing that franchises have to assess several factors rather than follow a fixed formula. According to him, recent performances, squad requirements and the quality of players available at the auction all influence such calls.

"It's very difficult to pinpoint the exact thought process behind the releases and retentions. It's obviously about performance, who the franchise values and who the franchise thinks is good enough to win cricket matches in the IPL. It is also about what's available at the auction. It's a small auction, so the franchise factors in the performance of the last two years and what it feels is required for the next three years. So, there is no thumb rule that this is right or that is wrong. It's just about faith and belief," he said.
Delhi have retained 16 players for the 2027 campaign, with Axar Patel, KL Rahul, Pant and Prithvi Shaw among the prominent Indian names in the group.

Their overseas contingent includes David Miller, Kyle Jamieson, Lungi Ngidi and Tristan Stubbs. The franchise has also retained a number of Indian players, including Sameer Rizvi, Ashutosh Sharma, Madhav Tiwari, Vipraj Nigam, Auqib Nabi, Mukesh Kumar, Tripurana Vijay and Zeeshan Ansari.
Among the notable departures are Nitish Rana, Karun Nair, Pathum Nissanka, Sahil Parakh, Ajay Mandal, Abhishek Porel, Dushmantha Chameera, Rehan Ahmed and Mitchell Starc.
Starc's release followed the Australian fast bowler informing both the franchise and the BCCI about his unavailability for IPL 2027, citing workload concerns.
Delhi will head into the December 16 mini-auction in Goa with nine slots to fill and Rs 39.50 crore remaining in their purse.

Meanwhile, Ganguly is looking forward to his new responsibility as Delhi Capitals head coach. Although he has previously been involved with the franchise in different capacities, the upcoming season will mark his first stint as head coach in the IPL.

He previously coached Pretoria Capitals last year and believes the IPL presents a different kind of challenge. Ganguly had earlier served as Delhi's Director of Cricket, overseeing several aspects of the franchise's operations during Ricky Ponting's tenure as head coach.

"It is my first time as head coach in the IPL. I did it for Pretoria Capitals last year, but I am very excited. The IPL is a very different challenge. I have been involved with DC in different ways, more so as the Director of Cricket, obviously organising everything when Ricky was the head coach. Now that I will be the head coach, I will be at the centre of taking this team forward," he said.

articles.headline: 'My goal is to go No. 1': Notre Dame senior Hannah Hidalgo out to prove she's the top pick in 2027 WNBA Draft
keyFacts: Notre Dame senior guard Hannah Hidalgo stated that her primary goal is to be selected as the number one overall pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft.
Hidalgo holds a strong basketball resume, having set the NCAA single-season steals record and multiple career statistical milestones.
Notre Dame has started the season with a 4-0 record and aims to make another deep tournament run with a largely new roster.
body: Hannah Hidalgo knows exactly what she is working toward during her senior year. Just a few days after the WNBA Draft Lottery, the Notre Dame senior made her goal clear.

"My goal is to go the highest pick. To go No. 1 and to whatever team, of course it's Toronto," Hidalgo told CBS Sports. "My goal is to go No. 1 and I'm going to do everything this season to show that I'm the No. 1 pick."

Most currently have Hidalgo at No. 2 or No. 3, while USC guard JuJu Watkins is the projected top pick. But a lot can happen between now and April, including Watkins deciding to stay one more year. Regardless of what Watkins decides, it's admirable that Hidalgo is doing what she can to control her own destiny.

At 5-foot-7, she is an undersized guard. However, her height has never stopped her from dominating on the court and her resume speaks for itself. Hidalgo plays like a "dawg" and has already earned the respect of basketball legends and Diana Taurasi.

Last season, Hidalgo set the NCAA single-season steals record with 202 steals and was named the Naismith Defensive Player of the Year. She has wasted no time this season as she already set another record by becoming the first college basketball player ever – men's or women's – to register at least 2,500 career points, 500 rebounds, 500 assists and 500 steals.
While she has big aspirations for draft night, Hidalgo is still focused on what she wants to accomplish during the last year of her college career.

"It's my senior year, so I think my sense of urgency is a lot bigger than what it has been," she said. "I'm excited. I think we have the pieces, even though we are young, we have the pieces to make it really far in the tournament and that's the goal."

Hidalgo led a virtually new roster to an improbable Elite Eight run last season and she is ready to run it back – even with yet another new set of teammates around her. Hidalgo, Leah Macy and Kelly Ratigan are the only returners, and Hidalgo is the only one who played in the tournament.

It is still early in the season and they haven't faced an AP Top 25 opponent yet, but the Fighting Irish are off to a promising 4-0 start. They have scored at least 99 points in all four wins, and with an average of 109.5 points per game, they have the second leading offense in the nation behind LSU.

Hidalgo is leading the country with 28.3 points per game, while also averaging a team-high 5.5 assists and 4.8 steals per contest. Her teammates are also holding their own as there are five other players averaging double figures, including sophomore Leah Macy who is averaging 23 points per contest. As the season continue to develop, Hidalgo is excited for the possibilities.
"We haven't even reached our ceiling," she said. "It's going to be a fun year."

articles.headline: Why GTA 6 doesn't have a 60 fps performance mode
keyFacts: Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 will target 30 frames per second across consoles at launch instead of offering a 60 fps mode.
Rockstar has historically released console games targeting 30 fps at launch, with few exceptions.
A PC port of GTA 6 is rumored for early 2027 and could potentially support higher frame rates with powerful hardware.
body: Why GTA 6 doesn't have a 60 fps performance mode
The biggest game of the year is only coming to consoles at launch.

GTA 6 is the most anticipated video game of all time. And it ain't close. I'll age myself hideously here, but the only handful of titles that have touched the same level of gaming hype in my four decades on this rock are Super Mario 64 (1996), the original Metal Gear Solid (1998), and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (also 1998).

There's no getting around it: GTA 6 may be the most important code in a box in the history of the medium. Oh, and if you're wondering, here's how long it will take you to download GTA 6. R.I.P. physical media. Unlike Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, there's no 60 frames per second (fps) mode in Rockstar's Vice City future mega hit.
Why won't GTA 6 play at 60 fps at launch?

60 fps is sadly off the table for the Leonida-set sandbox. I feel your pain. Rockstar recently confirmed GTA 6 is targeting 30 fps across consoles. At the time of pre-release writing, if the budget-focused Xbox Series S can hit that framerate reliably, I'll be extremely impressed.

This frame rate target is entirely in keeping with Rockstar's history. The iconic developer has never released a console game at launch that hit more than 30 fps, with one exception. The criminally forgotten, quietly excellent Rockstar Games Presents Table Tennis, back in 2006. PC ports of GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 could obviously exceed 60 fps with powerful enough hardware thrown at them — and plenty of post-launch patches. Yet in the console space, Rockstar has generally kept within 30 fps (again, at launch).

GTA 6 is a definite outlier for this console generation in terms of performance. On PS5 and Xbox Series X, many big-budget games offer 60 fps performance modes. Grand Theft Auto is probably the only video game franchise big enough to buck this frame-rate trend and get away with it.

What will 30 fps look like vs 60 fps in GTA 6? The simple answer is added input lag. I'm crossing my digits that the frame pacing of the biggest game of the generation will be consistent, which should hopefully provide a stable visual experience. Still, there's no question 60 fps normally feels vastly smoother than 30 fps gameplay.

In terms of input lag — the delay you can physically feel while holding a controller — we're talking 16.7ms vs 33.3ms. There's a reason 60 fps has become the default standard for this console generation: it's way smoother to play. I'd happily take an upscaled 1080p or 1440p title at 60 fps over a full-fat 4K game running at 30 fps.
What console will GTA 6 play best on?

If you're lucky enough to own a PS5 Pro, GTA 6 should look a whole lot better thanks to Sony's second stab at PSSR upscaling (that's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution, if you're not up to speed on your techy acronyms). Regardless of input lag on any of the consoles, it would be surprising if a game with likely the biggest budget of all time didn't hit an unprecedented level of image quality across platforms. But if you want the best experience, PS5 Pro is where it's at.

As for the gameplay on Xbox Series X and the base PS5? They'll likely look excellent, too. And don't discount the Series S, either. Microsoft's little white box actually has a CPU that's broadly similar to the one you'll find in the Series X. Will there be cutbacks to the GTA 6 experience on Series S? Almost certainly. Expect reduced crowds, draw distances and traffic. Still, despite the obviously lower resolution compared to the PS5 Pro, the general gameplay experience should be mostly the same.
Will the PC version of GTA 6 hit 60 fps?

There are whispers of a surprisingly early PC port of GTA 6 in the opening months of 2027. If that dream scenario does occur, a combination of NVIDIA's DLSS 4.5 Multi Frame Generation and VRR tech could allow for a 4K/120 fps Vice City experience. At launch, though, the best PS5 and Xbox Series X players can hope for is around 1440p at 30 fps, due to the relative weakness of console CPUs compared to cutting-edge PC silicon.

Rockstar has got me, though. I'm totally going to double dip when the game eventually lands on PC. I'm lucky enough to have only slightly overpaid for my NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090. If I sold it today — during these bleak AI data farm times — I'd triple my money on a card that should officially cost $1,9999. Paired with the current fastest gaming CPU on the market and 64GB of DDR5 RAM, my PC is the platform I ultimately want to experience GTA 6 on. I've been playing GTA 5: Enhanced Edition a lot lately at 4K/120 fps with all the ray-traced bells and whistles. I can't wait to do the same for its sequel.

articles.headline: Colts CB Justin Walley named the AFC defensive player of the week
keyFacts: Colts cornerback Justin Walley was named the AFC defensive player of the week on Wednesday.
Walley recorded five tackles, two tackles for loss, two passes defensed, and forced a fumble in the win over the Dolphins.
The award marks the first time a Colts player has won the honor since early in the 2024 season.
body: The Colts ended a five-game losing streak with last Sunday's win over the Dolphins and a defensive touchdown played a big role in the 24-22 win.

Cornerback Justin Walley got home on a blitz deep inside Miami territory and separated Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord from the ball. Defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore recovered the ball for a touchdown.
Walley had five tackles, two tackles for loss and two passes defensed overall in the win. The third-round pick has 40 tackles, two sacks and three forced fumbles to this point in his rookie season.
The NFL named Walley the AFC defensive player of the week on Wednesday. It's the first time a Colt has won the award since early in the 2024 season.

articles.headline: Former NFL star uses $54.6m career earnings to buy new football team that ‘merges two decorated clubs’
keyFacts: Former NFL player Justin Pugh announced that he has bought and merged two Italian football teams, the Seamen Milano and the Rhinos Milano, into a single entity called Dukes Milano.
Pugh, who became the Commissioner of the Italian Football League in February, acquired the teams through his business venture, the Milano American Football Company, in August.
The combined clubs will begin operating together at all levels starting in February 2027, coinciding with the next Italian Football League season.
body: Justin Pugh has announced that he has bought an American Football team in Italy.
The 36-year-old spent 11 years playing in the NFL as a guard after being selected by the New York Giants with the 19th overall pick in the 2013 draft.
Pugh spent 11 seasons in the NFL with the Giants and Cardinals Getty
Pugh spent the first six seasons of his career in New York before signing a five-year, $45 million deal with the Arizona Cardinals in 2018.
He spent the next five seasons in the Grand Canyon State but returned back to the Big Apple in 2023, playing a further 12 games for the G-Men.

He eventually called time on his career – where he earned approximately $54.6 million per Spotrac – in July 2025, almost two years after playing his last game in the NFL, doing so as a member of the Giants.

But it didn’t take long for Pugh to find his footing after retirement, with him announcing back in February of this year that he had assumed the role of the Commissioner of the Italian Football League (IFL).

His goal was simple – to grow the sport he had spent his childhood and early adulthood playing in Italy, with his connection to the European country stemming from his marriage to Italian-American Angela (Viscount) Pugh.

“American football has deep roots in Italy , and the passion this country has for the game is something truly special,” he stated at the time. “… I understand firsthand what this game demands, and more importantly, what it can give back.
“Football changed my life, and I have seen it transform communities, create opportunity, and build identity. Stepping into this role, my focus goes beyond competition. …

“Ambition alone is not enough,” he continued. “Structure must support it. Italy represents something unique in this landscape. It is a country synonymous with culture, design, excellence and global brand value.

“When American Football is developed with clarity, discipline and vision in this environment, it becomes more than a sport. It becomes a platform that blends athletic performance with cultural identity and international appeal.”
Pugh’s Italian Job sees two worlds collide
Pledging to “elevate the game in Italy with seriousness, ambition, and long term perspective”, Pugh has now revealed that two of the IFL’s biggest names have united as one.
Pugh became the Commissioner of the Italian Football League (IFL) in February Getty
View Tweet: https://t.co/6IsB4d26F5

The Seamen Milano and Rhinos Milano – which could perhaps best be likened to those more familiar with soccer, or football as it is known in Europe – as the IFL equivalent of Serie A juggernauts AC Milan and Inter Milan , have joined forces.
Now one entity, they will be known going forward as Dukes Milano.
“From the next step, the creation of this organization in Milan, the union of two existing ones,” Pugh said to La Gazzetta dello Sport.
“Last year, I served as commissioner and had the opportunity to closely observe the growth of the movement, the same growth that made me passionate about this sport in the first place.
“I thought: why not join forces? It might have seemed very complicated. It’s a bit like American football in the United States: imagine if the Jets and the Giants decided to collaborate.
“It seems impossible, but we put aside 50 years of rivalry to join forces. Fortunately, the presidents of both teams understood that, together, we can go much further.”
Pugh reportedly acquired and merged both teams through his business venture, the Milano American Football Company (MAFCo), first signing the agreement in August.

Starting in February 2027 – the start of the IFL season – every level of both former clubs, including the youth academies, senior tackle roster, and flag football programs will operate together, and as one.
It is expected that Pugh will continue to serve in his role as the IFL’s Commissioner and global ambassador.

articles.headline: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying
keyFacts: Developer TinyToad released a demo for Korridor, a game based on the vertical mobile shooter advertisements seen on YouTube.
The game features a slow-moving medieval monk who shoots enemies and navigates choice-driven gates that provide various buffs.
The reviewer stated that the game syncs enemy attacks with its soundtrack and allows players to defeat ogres.
body: I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!

Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.

Per the Steam page, it claims to have turned the above advert format into a whole new "deeply strategic genre", the "gates shooter", by stirring in "elements of roguelikes and bullet heavens". I need somebody to authenticate whether this is a truthful statement, or developer TinyToad pulling a fast one. In the meantime, I'll say that 1) I have now managed to kill several ogres, 2) I like Korridor's electro-metal soundtrack.

In Korridor, you're a bald medieval monk garbed in Poundshop Adeptus Astartes platemail. You've woken up in a dungeon of mysterious provenance, and must walk very slowly down its corridors korridors while shooting and punching goblins, wraiths and demons hurrying the other way. Each enemy has a numerical health indicator, and the basic challenge is working out whether you can empty it before they walk into you – which costs you a proportionate amount of health, mitigated by armour. As you go, you'll walk through a choice of gates that grant buffs such as faster health regen, bullet penetration, or nippier horizontal motion.

The fact that you don't control how fast the monk trudges vertically allows the game to synch the onslaught pretty tightly to the thudding, growling score. It reminds me a little of Thumper, though it isn't nearly so invigoratingly malevolent. So far. At intervals, the beat thickens and all the enemies burst into a sprint, throwing their arms up and conveying the strong impression that they are more running away from something than running at you. There's clearly a dreadful entity at the far end of the dungeon. Perhaps it is another overdressed monk with an even bigger gun.

Is this how those mobile games actually work? If it is, then alas and alack, all is lost. I've finally succumbed to those adverts, and all it took was some disingenuous Steam copy promising to place them at a critical remove. Curse you, TinyToad. Curse you and your gates. If you were actually a toad, I'd step on you. Still, now that we've broken the ice, can you please make another game in which I get to play one of those gloating giantesses in Hero Wars? Because I know some people who dig that kind of thing.

articles.headline: Wooting admits 'We found an issue with the Large Knob…'
keyFacts: Wooting co-founder and CEO Calder Limmen announced that the Large Knob has been delayed by up to four months to March 2027.
Limmen stated that 30% of the Large Knobs have an unexplained defect involving inaccurate testing and software representation values.
Wooting will investigate the issue over the next few months and ship orders earlier if the problem is resolved sooner.
body: So you may or may not have heard this, but Wooting has a Large Knob coming out soon. Think a traditional keyboard volume dial, but, yeah, large. And also available by itself without a keyboard. Well, Wooting opened up preorders for its $40/£34 Lekker Knob Large this year and the 80HE+, which was expected to launch in 2026, has now been pushed back to 2027. Big news, I know.

In a video titled "We found an issue with the Large Knob…", Wooting co-founder and CEO Calder Limmen announced that the Large Knob has been delayed by at most four months (it has moved back to March, 2027).
Limmen says he wanted to ship in December but "at the same time, I also had to make a decision and delay the Large Knob so that we don't ship a Large Knob with issues".

Limmen says 30% of the Large Knobs have a defect and they don't know why. They reportedly had a torque issue where larger production batches couldn't get the same level of resistance from each knob, which was then fixed by mounting the ball bearing inside the knob differently and changing some internals. But then, with the new batch, using a temperature chamber for testing, they spotted inaccurate testing in 30% of devices.

Effectively, the representation of the wheel in the software and the wheel itself had different values. If you simply have to swivel the wheel to use it, that wouldn't be a problem, but the Large Knob reportedly uses very specific movements in its software, so it needs absolute clarity over where exactly the dial is pointing.
That all means the next few months will involve Wooting engineers looking inside the Large Knob, performing more temperature tests and trying to figure out why this defect is happening.
Limmen also clarifies that if they figure out the problem much sooner, they will ship it earlier than January. The March 2027 release date is effectively a worst-case scenario.

As for those who have ordered the Large Knob, Wooting are handling the delays in different ways depending on how you ordered. If you picked up the Large Knob alongside a keyboard (other than the 80HE+, which comes with the knob built in), Wooting will ship the knob and keyboard separately, paying for the shipping. If you bought the keyboard with the built-in knob, it has also been delayed to March 2027, but will come with the travel case for free now.
If you bought the Large Knob by itself, you will get "some goodies [added] to your order." It's not clear yet what those goodies are, but a few extra is a nice way to make up for a delay.
